text: The additional-cost claim is carried on partner_instruction: result_code and fee_amount hold it, status holds its step, and its evidence file goes to rwb-document (P5). No cost table, no cost column and no migration is added.
why: The ownership rows give S9 three tables and list partner_instruction with DF-PRT-015 result_code and DF-PRT-016 fee_amount, and no source publishes a cost object or a cost table for the service.
read: TSD S9 T3.1 (partner, partner_instruction); context pack ownership rows (3 tables); TSD S9 T-A.2
applied_in: RWB-S9-E7017-APP s4, s11; RWB-S9-E7017-CON s11, s12.7
impact: A cost line that later needs its own fields becomes a new table and a new story; until then the claim is a result on the instruction and no schema change is needed.

text: The claim is recorded through API-S9-005 (Partner portal right U) and the fee invoice through API-S9-006 (right C); the approval and the refusal are a signal on InstructionWorkflow, because none of the six published operations of the module approves a claim.
why: TSD S9 T-A.1 publishes six operations and none of them approves or refuses; the context pack gives the service one workflow, InstructionWorkflow.
read: TSD S9 T-A.1, T-A.2; context pack ownership rows (6 provided, 1 workflow)
impact: The screen reaches the approval through the workflow signal and the composite route; no seventh operation and no approval route is invented.

text: The approval moves status to DONE and a refusal leaves it at IN_PROGRESS with the invoice blocked; the vocabulary stays LOV-INSTR-STATUS and no new state, list value or refusal reason code is invented.
why: DF-PRT-014 is bounded by LOV-INSTR-STATUS, which has no approved, refused or paid value, and no source gives a cost claim a state machine of its own.
read: TSD S9 T3.2; FSD S9 A2.14; legacy RWB-E7-017 screen and states table
impact: An approval is visible as DONE and a refusal as IN_PROGRESS with a blocked invoice, so the reason and the date of a refusal must be read from the decision record.

text: The held asset, its holding cost, the work order and the provision step stay with rwb-asset (S5, FEAT-AST-07), and the asset reference arrives on the instruction as an identifier. S9 holds no v_ace_* grant, so DP-05 is applied as a prohibition rather than a read.
why: The legacy data section reads v_ace_npa_asset, but the ownership rows give that view to P1 and the asset record to S5, the plan's contract-dependency row is empty, and the service holds no ACE grant in the realignment.
read: Legacy RWB-E7-017 data table (DF-ACE-208 to DF-ACE-219); context pack ownership rows; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-05
impact: The asset fields are evidenced only through rwb-asset's contract and its screens, and a story that needs an asset field opens a contract dependency with S5.

text: The partner-portal right of a caller is enforced by the platform guard, and no rwb-access operation is declared as a contract row of this key because the plan's contract-dependency row is empty and DP-08 is not in its pattern set.
why: The metadata rows of both stories carry no contract dependency, while TSD S9 T6.1 and T6.2 require a right per operation and a scope filter; the guard is a capability of the service template.
read: TSD S9 T6.1, T6.2; plan rows for RWB-S9-E7017-APP and RWB-S9-E7017-CON
impact: The right check is proved on the guard fake; if rwb-access must be a declared dependency, a C row and a fake are added without changing the operations.

text: EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted announces the recorded claim, once per claim, with caseId, instructionId, resultCode and resultedAt; no invoice event and no approval event is published because the service's pair has none.
why: TSD S9 T5.3 publishes InstructionIssued and PartnerResultSubmitted only, and the ownership rows give the service two events.
read: TSD S9 T5.3; context pack events (EV-20, EV-21)
applied_in: RWB-S9-E7017-APP s2, s4, s12.3; RWB-S9-E7017-CON s12.3
impact: Downstream services learn of a claim through EV-21 and of an approval only by reading the instruction; a consumer that needs an approval event is a new story and an Arch change.

text: The fee schedule the claim is checked against is versioned reference data of the partner panel held with S9's own rows (FEAT-PRM-02); no reference-data contract row is declared because DP-07 is not in the pattern set.
why: FSD S9 A2.2 makes the panel, the fee schedule and the service levels versioned reference data of the module, and neither metadata row carries a reference-data dependency.
read: FSD S9 A2.2, A2.14; REQ-S9-004; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-07
impact: The check compares the claimed amount with the schedule version in force; if the schedule becomes rwb-case reference data, a C row and a fake are added.

text: Wave 4 and business epic EP07 agree with the service's Arch v5 wave 4, and the release stays 31 May 2027 (tentative) copied unchanged.
why: Template and Rules §R5.6 maps EP07 to wave 4 and the service table gives S9 wave 4, so no W-MAP conflict arises and no date may be changed or raised as a gap.
read: Template and Rules §R5.6, §R1 (U7); context pack service row (wave 4); legacy RWB-E7-017 epic row
impact: None; the release date stays tentative and no conflict gap is raised for this service and epic.
